item.title: Nominations open for PEI Anti-Racism Recognition Award
item.description:
Nominations open for PEI Anti-Racism Recognition Award jpranahan Fri, 11/13/2026 - 12:15

Island residents are invited to nominate individuals, community groups and organizations that are making a difference in addressing racism and promoting racial equity across Prince Edward Island. 

The Anti-Racism Recognition Award recognizes leadership, advocacy and community efforts that help remove barriers, promote inclusion and create positive change for racialized and Indigenous communities.

Nominations are open until December 14, 2026 at 11:59 p.m. AST.

Individuals, community groups and organizations may be nominated for their contributions to advancing anti-racism, racial equity, inclusion or reconciliation in Prince Edward Island.

The award was established through the Anti-Racism Action Plan for Prince Edward Island 2023-2028 as part of the province’s commitment to recognizing efforts to address racism.

The inaugural award was presented in February 2026 to Tamara Steele, former executive director and board member of the Black Cultural Society of PEI, in recognition of her longstanding leadership, advocacy and contributions to racial justice on the Island. 

To learn more about the eligibility criteria or to submit a nomination, visit here.

For questions about the award or nomination process, contact the Anti-Racism Office at antiracismtable@gov.pe.ca.

item.title: Islanders invited to submit input on codes of conduct for Island schools
item.description:
Islanders invited to submit input on codes of conduct for Island schools jenniferdhogan Thu, 11/12/2026 - 15:04

Islanders have an opportunity to help shape new codes of conduct for Island schools to support safe, respectful learning environments across the province. 

Public consultations are underway at both the Public Schools Branch (PSB) and La Commission scolaire de langue française (CSLF) as each organization develops their own code and asks Islanders for input. 

Creating new codes of conduct was a key recommendation in the Jenkins Report, Student Safety in Island Schools: Handling of Complaints and Incidents of Staff Sexual Misconduct. In response, the Minister of Education and Early Years issued a ministerial directive in September, with education authorities expected to approve the new codes by the end of 2026.

Provide input on the PSB code of conduct by visiting the PSB website.

Provide input on the CSLF code of conduct, visit the CSLF website.

The deadline for submissions is December 12, 2026.

Quotes:

“These new codes of conduct will set shared expectations for students, staff, parents and guardians, volunteers and visitors, and will help encourage positive behaviour. They will also help ensure consistency from school to school, so expectations do not change as students and families move through the PSB and CSLF. I encourage all Islanders to provide input to help shape the new codes.”

 - Minister of Education and Early Years Robin Croucher

“A code of conduct developed by and for La Commission scolaire de langue française will reflect the reality, aspirations, and identity of our school community. It will provide a common framework for promoting respectful and positive relationships throughout our community, helping ensure the well-being and success of everyone.”

  - CSLF Superintendent Ghislain Bernard

"Feeling safe, respected, and supported through positive interactions is how students thrive in our schools and at home. A clear, consistent expectation through a common code of conduct helps make that possible by giving students, staff, and families a common understanding of how we treat one another and our surroundings. We want this code to reflect the voices of our school communities, so I urge students, families, and staff to share their thoughts on the codes."

- PSB interim director Rob MacAdam

item.title: Six decades together and able to stay at home with the right support
item.description:
Six decades together and able to stay at home with the right support jenniferdhogan Thu, 11/12/2026 - 10:14

For Stanley and Adrienne MacDonald, home is a place filled with love, laughter, and memories. Their house in O'Leary was built in 1914 and once belonged to Adrienne's grandparents. 

The couple brought it back into the family in 1970 and raised their three daughters, Heidi, Bethany, and Jill. Now 84 and 82, Stanley and Adrienne celebrated 60 years of marriage this past year. Their home is filled with family photographs and reminders of the life they've built together.

Looking back on six decades of marriage, Stanley jokes about reaching the milestone. "We didn't think we'd make it," he says with a laugh.

They've shared plenty of adventures over the years, including cruises around the world. Stanley, a retired pharmacist who spent his career at the O’Leary Pharmacy, keeps busy offering private tours of the Island to visiting cruise ship passengers. These days, much of his time is spent caring for Adrienne. 

As her health and mobility have changed, Stanley has become her primary caregiver. With additional help from caregivers coming into their home each day, he's able to make sure Adrienne gets the care she needs.

"We have a schedule," Stanley says. "I'm more on duty at night and some of the day in the mornings, depending on what help is available that day."

The couple recently began receiving financial support through the province's At Home Caregiver Benefit, which helps eligible Islanders with high care needs continue living at home with the support of a primary caregiver.

Adrienne recently spent nearly two weeks in hospital. While her stay helped address some health concerns, she was eager to get back home and be surrounded by familiar comforts.

The couple has adapted their home to meet Adrienne's needs, turning a downstairs room into a bedroom and adding a wheelchair ramp. Caregivers help with meals, personal care and other daily tasks, while Stanley looks after her medications.

Their eldest daughter Heidi, who lives in New Brunswick, helped arrange the benefit and, along with her sisters Bethany in England and Jill in British Columbia, remains closely involved in coordinating her parents' care. Regular FaceTime calls and visits help keep the family connected.

"Dad has always been very independent and he's doing everything he can to make sure Mom is comfortable and well cared for,” Heidi says. “Having that extra support makes a big difference. It means they can stay at home together, with Dad’s bed right next to hers.” “Thankfully, Mom is almost always smiling and still makes jokes,” she adds. 

Stanley says they didn't initially realize they could get financial assistance to help with the cost of care.
"We had no idea this kind of financial help was available," he says. "It does cost a lot when you're bringing in people to help every day. It means we can keep things going here at home."

The At Home Caregiver Benefit provides eligible households with between $250 and $1,500 per month, depending on household income, to help with the cost of caring for a loved one.

For Stanley and Adrienne, the benefit is helping make it possible to continue the life they've built together in the place they've called home for more than 50 years.

After 60 years of marriage, Stanley knows Adrienne pretty well. Their days may look different now, but what matters most has not changed.

"The key word is comfort and happiness," he says. "That makes it so much easier for us, to know that she's comfortable and still smiling."
 

For more information, visit At Home Caregiver Benefit.

item.title: Premier McLeod on the Enbridge Line 21 Pipeline
item.description:
YELLOWKNIFE - Premier Bob McLeod issued the following statement on the Enbridge Line 21 pipeline today:

“I was pleased to learn that operations have resumed for Enbridge’s Line 21 pipeline after almost 2 years of no activity.

"Resource development has, and will continue to be, the backbone of our economy and is central to ensuring a good source of middle class jobs and business opportunities. Our territory has mineral and petroleum resources and the development of those resources can have a transformative effect on our people and economy.

"Sustainable economic development is key to the future of Northerners. With a strong resource development base, we will be able to support diversification of our local economies into emerging and established sectors.

"On behalf of the Government of the Northwest Territories I’d like to offer my congratulations to Imperial Oil, Enbridge the town of Norman Wells and other partners for getting this pipeline back up and running. I know the efforts and economic impacts of the pipeline have already begun to take shape in the community and will be felt for years to come. ”

 

Charlotte Digness
Media and Communications Coordinator
Cabinet Communications and Protocol
Government of the Northwest Territories
